title.narrative: Advancing Lifelong STEM Skills Development for Youth and Adults

description.narrative:
Rapid advances in science, technology, artificial intelligence, automation and the transition towards greener economies are transforming labour markets and societies at an unprecedented pace. Increasingly, young people and adults need opportunities to continuously develop and update their knowledge and skills in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) to access decent work, adapt to changing career pathways, participate in innovation, and contribute to sustainable development. Evidence from international organizations highlights growing demand for STEM-related skills across sectors, while many countries continue to face significant shortages of qualified workers and unequal access to learning opportunities, particularly for women and disadvantaged groups.
In response, the activities will support the advancement of lifelong STEM skills development opportunities for youth and adults through research, capacity development, advocacy and partnerships. The activities under this workplan will generate evidence on emerging STEM skills needs and effective practices, facilitate knowledge sharing among stakeholders, and strengthen capacities to promote inclusive and relevant STEM learning opportunities throughout life. Particular attention will be given to gender equality, digital transformation, green transitions and expanding participation in STEM learning and careers.
Initial funding will provide seed support to launch key activities, establish partnerships, develop knowledge products and initiate capacity-development efforts. These resources will enable UNESCO to lay the foundations for a broader programme of work and demonstrate impact in priority areas. The scope and scale of implementation will be further expanded through the mobilization of additional voluntary contributions and strategic partnerships, allowing successful initiatives to reach more beneficiaries and countries.
Key deliverables, subject to available resources, may include a mapping of promising practices and trends in lifelong STEM skills development; a knowledge product with recommendations for policymakers and practitioners; capacity-development activities for relevant stakeholders; and awareness-raising and partnership-building initiatives to promote access to STEM learning opportunities for youth and adults. Through these actions, the project will contribute to expanding participation in STEM learning, strengthening career pathways, and fostering innovation, resilience and sustainable development.
